raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? I noticed that people in the 18 to 29 were the group most in favor of college athletes being paid. And as each group get's older in age, they are less in favor of college athletes being paid. This is likely due to younger generations siding with student athletes their age, while older age groups are sticking to more traditional ideas. 

2. What do you wonder? I wonder why so many more men think college athletes should be paid than women. If I had to guess, this might be because men are more likely to be invested in money dominant sports like football and basketball. I also wonder how many people on the graph were athletes in high school and college. I think someones athletic background is essential to this topic, as someone with no interest in sports may not be sure. 

3. What impact does this have you and your community? Even though I don't think I will play competitive sports in college, being a high school athlete has shown me how much dedication and hard work it takes to be an athlete. I have friends and family who are or have played college sports at a high level, and that commitment is on a whole other level. With all the hard work college athletes put in, they deserve to be rewarded.

4. What's going on in the graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.
The graph is measuring the background and demographics of people who do or do not think college athletes should be paid. 
Should College Athletes be Paid?

raw_comment:
. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, wherein the graph is the evidence to support it?

Younger people favor paying college athletes more than older age groups. This is shown with the drastic difference between the age group of 18-29 vs. the age group of 60+.

2. What do you wonder?

Why do the older people who were surveyed not support college athletes being paid? The same type of question for the women who favor athletes not being paid. Why is there such a change between males and females if both participate in college athletics? 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?

In my community, athletics are highly participated in by age levels ranging from 5-18+. When these sports get more serious in high school years, people may be less inclined to continue them into college if they don't receive payment for them. In some cases, I understand that athletes may receive a full ride or lesser tuition than others. But, this is not the case for every player.

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

Payment Is Highly Encouraged by Younger Americans for College Athletics

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?

I notice that people within the 18-29 age range for the most part strongly agree that college athletes should be paid. As you move up you can notice that this view shifts in the opposite direction, as 60% of participants in the 60 or older age range believe that college athletes should not be paid. I also notice that white people, as well as women, and senior citizens also seem to lean towards the idea of college athletes not being paid.

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder if there are different societal pressures and expectations among all these groups of people and how that may affect their opinions on whether or not college athletes should be paid. I also wonder if racial minorities vote higher on paying athletes due to wage discrimination and the upsetting history that our country has when it comes to the topic of race and pay equality.

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
While I don’t plan on becoming a college athlete, I have many friends and peers who see themselves playing a sport in college. Payment for college athletes could have an impact on the expenses that they may have to pay for potential injuries as well as helping to minimize the amount of college debt that the student will have to pay off post-college. 

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

“College Athletes: Pay or No Play”

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence supported?
I noticed that those who are around the age of starting or going to college agree that College Athletes should get paid. I notice how as the age goes up, people lean towards no. I also noticed how when it comes to Race/Ethnicity that out of the 3 listed, Black and Latino lean more towards saying that college athletes should get paid, rather than Whites who lean more towards no.

2.What do you wonder?
I wonder why when the age group goes up, they lean towards no. I also wonder why more women voted no rather then yes, It feels like something women would agree that colleges should do, I'm curious about that. Also I wonder why out of the 3 races, white people voted no the most.

3. What impact does this have on you and your community? As much as an impact and opportunity this would have on kids who cannot afford a high costing tuition for college's, I personally will not (I'm sure of it) be participating in any sports on college. But of course if you are going to college only for a sport, I'd hope the college would pay you.

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graphs main idea.
"We get entertainment, but they don't get paid? Where's the money going??" 
This graph represents peoples opinions on College athletes being paid.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?
I notice that the people who are going through the college process would agree that college athletes should be paid. People of the older generation lean more against this idea - and I conclude that it is because of the change in tuition for college. When people at age 60 went to college, tuition was several thousand dollars cheaper. Now, it is around 70k a year for a lot of schools around America. 

2. What do you wonder?
I wonder if the athletic associations like NFL and NHL would have more recognition and better players if they offered money to college athletes. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
I think that there are plenty of opportunities to lower the cost of college tuition through scholarships and taking advantage of optional work. I don't plan on doing a sport in college so this wouldn't necessarily affect me personally. However, for those that are only going to college for a sport - this may be a better option. 

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.
Should college athletes get paid as professional athletes? A lot of college athletes are more focused on the athletic rigor and commitment that comes with playing for a college team rather than academics.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I notice that the age, race and gender have a direct correlation on what people answered.

The older people were, the more likely they were to say “no, college athletes should not be paid”.

People of color were more likely to say “yes, college athletes should be paid”. 

Men said that college athletes should be paid.

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder if the reason that the people in the older category said no, college athletes should not be paid because of more traditionalist values and ideas. 

I wonder how the statistics would change if the college sport in question was specified

I wonder how much the economic state of the people being asked affects the answers they give

I wonder how political opinions affect the answers. Is the reason there are more older people saying no to paying college athletes because older generations tend to be more conservative compared to younger generations?

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This could impact people because college is expensive. If athletes could sustain themselves or even pay off college using a salary from playing the sport they play, which is basically a job on its own, instead of having jobs on the side getting in the way of studying and their sport, it could be very beneficial. 

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

Is Education Not Enough Compensation? Why Should College Athletes Be Paid?

I notice that the older the people surveyed got the more percent of them voted no. I also notice more men agree that athletes should get paid more.

I wonder if these votes are persuaded by whether or not these people are relegated to, were or are currently a college athlete.

This doesn’t affect me personally but as many of my peers are starting to apply to college some are being scouted by colleges to continue and play at their school, this may have an impact on their future if they choose to start paying college athletes.

1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?

I noticed that as the ages of the people surveyed increased, not only did the amount of "Unsure" votes increase, but the amount of "No" votes increased in regard to whether college athletes should be paid or not. My claim can be supported by the first section of the graph which is labeled "Age."

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder if the reason why people who are older in particular tend to be indifferent or against colleges paying their student-athletes is because they aren't student-athletes themselves and, therefore, think it is unnecessary to potentially "waste" money on something that does not need it. I just wonder what the reasons were for the votes. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?

This does not affect me directly. However, this could possibly impact some of my classmates in the near future. I am unaware of how important this topic is to current athletes at Andover High School and others in the community.

4. What's going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

There are only a few specific categories that certain groups agree on.

Headline: "Who should we really be asking for whether student-athletes should receive compensation or not?"

raw_comment:
I notice that the younger the audience, the more they believe that colleges should pay their athletes. In the age category of the graph, in the range of 18-24, 70% believe that colleges should pay their athletes. This is the majority of the vote, whereas in the age group of 60 or older, 60% of the votes were for no.
I wonder, if college athletes were to be paid, how much would they be paid? And how would it be calculated? (By game played, hours, effort, star players, etc.)

This graph has a large impact on the sports community overall, and it could affect where fellow students at AHS are planning to go (if at all) to college. Personally, if I were playing a sport for a college regardless, I would much rather be paid than not. This may be a deciding factor for some individuals. This may also eliminate the need for a part-time job in college and allow the student to fully focus on sports.

Debt or Defeat: Should Colleges Be Paying Their Athletes?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
As people get older, I observe that they believe colleges shouldn't pay their athletes as much as younger people. Non-white people are more in favor of colleges paying their athletes. White folks, who do not concur, favor the opposite.Compared to women, more males believe that athletes should be compensated. I also observed that more persons than any other group chose "yes" for the age range of 18 to 29 years old, while a smaller proportion chose "yes" for the age range of 60 years or older.

What do you wonder?
These graphs make me question whether colleges began paying their athletes as a result, and I also wonder why so few individuals believed that elderly athletes (60 years old or older) shouldn't be paid. And why, despite receiving the best benefits, the men who play collegiate basketball want to get compensated. such being a scholarship that is unpaid. (include shelter and food) If they eat and sleep at the dorm, you don't need to give them money.

How does this relate to you and your community?
Because athletes who desire to continue playing their sport in college are likely to dedicate their lives to it and sacrifice other aspects of their schedules, I believe this has an impact on both me and my community. They won't have any chance to find work to support themselves if they must attend school and play sports full-time.

What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

Why Play If Not Paid ?

raw_comment:
1.	It appears that the younger you are, the more you believe college athletes should get paid. White people, women, and senior citizens are all least likely to believe college athletes deserve a salary. It appears that most people however seem to believe college athletes should be paid.
2.	I wonder if the societal impact upon these groups of people affects their opinions on the matter. With age comes experience, so maybe older people do not believe college athletes should be paid because experience has taught them that they do not deserve it. Perhaps the racial minorities voting higher could be due to the fact that it’s hard enough for them to make money as it is being a racial minority in America, where it’s statistically harder to get jobs and higher salaries.
3.	Many people around me are going to play college football. Whether or not they are paid or compensated could make a huge difference in their careers. This could also affect the gambling in our town, as there is a lot of gambling, even on sports—though it is technically illegal outside of authorized locations.

This also relates to me, because I am part of the majority that believe they should actually get paid.

This relates to me as I am an athlete that is looking to play sports in college and would like to be paid as I play as college athletics is essentially a full-time job, especially for football.

What do you notice?
I'm noticing that young people are more biased towards athletes being paid, and are also usually more sure of their decisions about it than their older counterparts!

What do you wonder?
I'm wondering what's causing the variation in responses from Black, Latino, and white participants. Could it possibly be because of differences in how sports is integrated into their cultures?
I also want to see these people's opinions on paying college students for other extracurriculars that get shown to the public-- such as performing arts like music groups who perform concerts or theater groups that bring in income from shows! Since these aren't nearly as integrated into modern culture as sports, I think it'd be interesting to see how people view these compared to sports.

How does this relate to you and your community?
Maybe this is a bit of a stretch, but I am finding it interesting how there's a pattern where old people don't want to pay young people. It's visible in this graph, but also in the workplace now.

What’s going on in this graph?

Something I noticed is the steady decrease in percentages that said yes depending on age. The reason for this is because as age increases there are different generations that are being surveyed which means different morals/views.

How does this relate to your community?
This relates to my community because there are numerous colleges that are in my area which this may effect. This also effects me because I am attending college next year and am looking to play a sport. 

Headline?
Athletes paid by skill, or should they be?

raw_comment:
1) I've noticed that elderly individuals tend to disagree with universities paying their players. Votes that universities shouldn't pay their athletes rise as people get older. Most likely because the issue is most pertinent to them and student-athletes of that age group and would be most advantageous to them, the category 18-29 has the largest percentage of respondents who believe universities should pay their players. The least number of those voting "no" are in the 60+ age group. They also have the greatest number of "unsure" voters. This is probably because collegiate athletics are not popular among persons in that age group. I also see that more white voters than other ethnic groups and more female voters than male voters declined to participate in the poll.

2) I'm curious as to why more white people declined than Black or Latino people. I would have wanted to see the outcomes for voters from various socioeconomic backgrounds.

3) Because I am at the age where college sports recruiting is most common, I can most directly connect to this. I am familiar with numerous folks my age who have recently made commitments or are now seeking employment.

4) Play or Pay.

1. I notice that there are bigger percentages of the students saying yes rather than no. I also noticed little to none were not sure about the question asked. The graph is also divided into different groups, age, race, and gender. 

2. I wonder how come a great percentage of elders, women, and white people are against college paying their athletes. If they were athletes in college, wouldn't they want to get paid for what they play? Wouldn't it be some sort of "reward" for all the efforts they put into the sport and it could kick off their career while also making a living in a way throughout college. 

3. This relates to me and my community because I know a few kids want to move onto playing sports in college or some have already. And I'm curious to see how they may feel about this poll. 

4. This graph is divided into three categorical groups (age, race, gender) to determine what each group votes regarding whether or not college athletes should get paid by the school they play/go to.

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice? I notice that most adults believe that the younger generation of athletes should get paid by colleges. The percentage is significant, 70% of adults think colleges should pay their athletes from ages 18 to 29. The other age groups are either 50/50 or more adults who think colleges shouldn’t pay their athletes.

2) What do you wonder? I wonder why more adults think the athletes that are minorities should get paid by their colleges than white athletes. I wonder if it has to do with the fact that the minorities do not have as many resources as white people do. There are many athletes with potential but are limited which deprives them from becoming professionals.

3) How does this relate to you and your community? This relates to me and my community because I live in an area that is home to mostly hispanics. My hispanic peers and myself are incredibly talented like any other race. Yet money is still a major factor in everything we do. I see many of my peers who would like to do more but face limitations due to their status. When given the opportunity they are able to reach their full potential. An example of this is financial aid for upcoming college students, this paves the way for many people who would like to pursue an education but do not possess the money themselves to fully pay for college.

raw_comment:
1. I notice that there is a higher percentage of younger age groups who believe that colleges should pay their athletes compared to older age groups. Also, looking at the race/ethnicity category, more blacks and latinos agree that colleges should pay their athletes, while white people have a higher percentage that say no instead of yes. And men are more likely to think colleges should pay their athletes than women. 

2. I wonder why each time the age group gets older the less they say yes and if those people were athletes or even like sports. Also, why are there less white people that say yes compared to blacks and latinos, and if most of them were non athletes. I wonder what caused women to say no if there are sports that they can play, could it be because there are more sports for men than for women?

3. This relates to my community because it is diverse and there are many athletes that I know are deciding to continue playing at college, and I know many would like to get paid by the college because it would help them a lot. 

4. This graph is showing three categories, age, race/ethnicity, and gender and each of them show different percentages that help us compare them.

raw_comment: I notice that younger people tend to say yes, as well as minority groups and men. I wonder if this has to do with more minority groups and younger people actually playing college sports and therefore want to be paid since they're already playing either way. I also notice that the older people get, the more they tend to say no, that could be because some of the people were college athletes themselves and want to keep the rules the same way since they didn't get paid either and would rather that no one gets paid as well. This relates to me and my community because I know kids that have a very good chance of becoming college athletes and would like them to succeed and gain money for their efforts. Since they're giving a hundred percent of their time and body for their sport, and deserve to be rewarded, especially since making money is easier than ever for young people and they're choosing to spend all their time in a sport. raw_comment:
1. I noticed that younger people tend to think that athletes should be paid, while the older population thinks that they should not. I also noticed that it was more likely for men to agree that college athletes should be paid rather than women. Additionally, the black and latino communities tended to agree more than white. 
2. I wonder why the older generations do not support the paying of college athletes. And, I wonder if they comprehend the struggle  it must be to have to be a full-time athlete as well as a full-time student!
3. This relates to me as I am an athlete who is looking to play in college, and a lot of my friends are as well. I believe personally that college athletes should be paid, for they are playing for their school at a very high level plus attending classes like the normal college student. While some may get scholarships, not everyone does, therefore I believe there should be some sort of outcome from playing on a college team. 
4. A good headline idea could be "Pay to Play?"

raw_comment: I noticed many different things while I analyzed this graph. First of all, in the survey, it was found that a majority of men supported the idea of pay for college athletes while only 39% of women chose to support pay for college athletes. It was interesting to see that a much larger amount of blacks and Latinos surveyed believed that colleges should pay athletes compared to only 34% of whites. A much larger portion of younger people was supportive for pay college athletes. I wonder if these younger participants recent experiences in college contributed in their decision to support pay for college athletes. I also wonder if men were more supportive in pay for college athletes because men tend to be generally more interested in sports as a whole and because a majority of college athletes are male. This relates to my community because many of my peers and I are beginning to consider college options and sports benefits may influence our choices.

raw_comment:
1. Participants who are closer in age to those of college athletes were more likely to support the idea that college athletes should be paid. The graph also reflects that men are more likely agree that college athletes should be paid rather than women. It also shows that people with the ethnicity of Black and Latino feel that college athletes should be paid. 
2. I wonder how many respondents are or were college athletes. I also wonder why opinions on colleges paying their athletes varied depending on the gender and ethnicity of respondents, especially because in these times women are fighting for equal pay. 
3. In my community, I know many student athletes who are committed to playing sports in college. From their experiences, I know it is a lot to be a college student athlete, managing their studies while also committing to their sport. These athletes play for their school, who benefits from them especially if they win. Knowing that a lot of that money isn’t going to athletes who have worked exceptionally hard to put themselves out there to be the best that they can be is unfair. 
4. “Paid for play”

raw_comment:
Based on the statistics, I noticed that 60% of people aged over 45 along with 60% of the white population believe colleges should not pay their athletes. 

I wonder why people believe this . . . college athletes should not have to wait to join notorious leagues to get paid money for their expertise. Student-athletes hinder their educational process to focus more on their physical attributes and athletic status. All the while, these scholars are representing the colleges they are situated in. Due to this, many factors may go as far as suggesting colleges "abuse" student-athletes of their time and money.

While this does not affect my community specifically, scholars who apply to colleges to profess their abilities should be rewarded in some of the compensation.

The graph indicates a poll on whether or not colleges should pay their student-athletes. A catchy title may be "Census Poll - Should college-athletes be paid?"

raw_comment:
1. This graph shows the data of what people think about the topic, separated between race, gender, and age. Between yes and no there are still some people that are unsure. Yet it is hard to tell how many people are unsure in total because the figures don't add up to 100. In age: 18-44 more than 50% say yes to athletes who should get paid by their college.  45-60 both have 60% that say no to athletes getting paid. With this I can tell more younger people agree with rather than the older people who disagree. In race: Both Black and Latino have 70% of people who agree. On the other hand White people have 60% who disagree. In gender: More than 50% male agree while more than 50% of women disagree. More men are saying yes to athletes getting paid, this could lead into having more male athletes. 
2. I wonder if this information is based on the people in college or if they did go to college. Not only this but if it was asked to athletes as well. Also if this was asked to not only athletes, but a family member of an athlete. This can create a biased opinion. 
3. This relates to the community by benefitting low income communities. When athletes come from a low income community they would be able to benefit from being paid by their college. Their family will also benefit from this. By providing money for them they will be guaranteed good resources, supplies, and health. 
Headline: Should Colleges Pay Up to Their Athletes?

raw_comment:
1. I notice that 70% of the younger population (18-29 years) agree that college athletes should be paid. However the older population ( 45-59 & 60+ years) both have 60% of their populations agree that college athletes shouldn't be paid. The population of blacks and Latin are each 69% of who agree athletes should be paid. While 60% of whites think they shouldn't be paid. And more men (54%) agree that college athletes compared to women (39%).

2. I wonder how people decide if these college athletes should be paid or not. And I also wonder why the older generations disagree with college athletes getting paid and why more of the younger generation agrees.

3. This relates to my community because there are many people who would like to pursue sports in their future and would like to attend college to do sports.  

4. College Athletes: To be paid or not?

raw_comment:
I noticed that young male Black and Latino participants favored colleges paying their athletes more than the other participants did. I believe it's because this demographic tends to depend on college sports to support their educations, so they personally benefit from athletes being paid.

I wonder why so many women answered no to the survey. Although the college sport community  tends to be dominated by men, there are many skilled female athletes that could benefit from being paid for their work so I would've assumed there would have been more women who were for the cause.

This doesn't relate to me personally, seeing as I'm not a serious athlete, nor am I close to anyone who seeks to be one. However, I am aware that within my community, there are many teens who look forward to playing sports in college and they are most likely to be very passionate on this subject.

In the graph, we see the opinions of different demographics on the topic of college athletes being paid, and there are a few simple conclusions that can be drawn from it. One headline that would go well with this graph is "Colleges Profit off of D1 Sports. Should the Athletes Get a Cut?"

raw_comment:
I notice that a majority of people who voted yes to paying athletes are young adults, people of black or latino race, and men. I also notice that as the age increases more people voted no than yes. Most of the population that voted that they were unsure were 60 or older,  white or black, and women. 

I wonder if the majority that voted yes to paying athletes are athletes themselves. I also wonder why less women votes yes to paying them due to the fact that many female sports dont receive as much attention as male sports. I wonder why more elderly people and older people in general think that athletes shouldnt be paid. 

This related to me and my community because many women voted no to paying athletes. The female population that voted no represents our community. This also relates to my community because there are many women that play sports as well as me and some are effected by the fact that athletes are unpaid.

"play for money or play for nothing?"

raw_comment:
I noticed that younger age groups, like 18 to 29, and 30 to 44, believe colleges should pay their athletes. I also take note of the fact that the older the age group the more people believe colleges should not pay their athletes. In all age groups, there is a very slim group of people who are unsure in regard to the question. As for race and ethnicity, POC (blacks and latinos) have a higher percentage of people who think colleges should pay their athletes. While, whites more likely believe they shouldn't. Pertaining to gender, men mostly answered yes. Women mostly answered no. 

 I wonder why older age groups answered no. Were sports less of a big deal? Does it have to do with the fact that things were much cheaper back then? Does it have to do with certain beliefs? And as for gender, why did more women answer no than yes? Could it have to do with the fact that female athletes get paid less than male athletes?

Although Perth Amboy isn't really known for sports, we do have a lot of athletes that have potential (individually), a lot of kids want to continue their athletic careers in college. And I know how much they get paid will influence a lot of their decisions and commitments and either help them financially or not. Most of us come from low income homes, so we would most likely agree to college athletes getting paid/

raw_comment: 1. I noticed that the younger demographic believes that college athletes should be paid while the older members believe that they should not be paid. Minorities also agree with the idea of colleges paying their athletes while the majority of white people disagree. Men also seem to agree that the athletes deserve pay while the majority of women beg to differ. I wonder if the people surveyed understood how hard it must be for college athletes, to not only play the sport and show up to practices but also maintain a social life and keep their grades up. Many college athletes also don't have enough time to work and save up money for when they leave college and might leave in debt although they put in hard work and have their names and images used by the schools. This is not a significant issue that I personally must deal with, but I understand that people in my community may suffer from the unpaid burden these sports can sometimes present. The graph is showing a survey of people opinions on whether colleges should pay colleges and a catchy headline would be "Should Students Be Paid to Play?"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that older people generally do not think colleges should pay their athletes. As age increases, votes saying colleges should not pay their athletes increase. The category 18-29 has the highest amount of people saying colleges should pay their athletes, most likely because the question is most relevant to them and student-athletes that age and it would benefit them most. The age range of 60+ has the lowest amount of votes saying no. They also have the largest range of people who voted “unsure”. This is likely due to people of that age range being uninvolved in college sports. I also notice that more white voters said no to the poll than other ethnicities and more women said no to the poll than men. 
What do you wonder?
I am most curious about the disparity in votes between races. I wonder why more whites said no than the Black or Latino groups. I would have liked to see the results for voters across multiple income levels. 
How does this relate to you?
This relates most to me because I am at the age where college recruitment for sports is most prevalent. I know many people my age who have recently committed or are in the recruitment process currently. 
A catchy headline for this graph would be “Is a Full Ride Enough?”

raw_comment:
1. One thing I noticed was that there is a larger amount of younger people agreeing with the statement that colleges should pay their athletes.

2. I wonder what goes through peoples heads, that think college athletes shouldn’t get payed. They play for a big audience, that generates a lot of revenue from ticket sales. They deserve to get a chunk of profits just like NBA players do.

3. This relates to me and my community, because there are athletes that I know that want to go to college for sports.

4. The graph shows the percentage of people who vote in favor or against athletes being paid in college. It is also based on their age,ethnicity, and gender. 
Headline: Should College players get a salary?
ace_sentences: One thing I noticed was that there is a larger amount of younger people agreeing with the statement that colleges should pay their athletes.
I wonder what goes through peoples heads.
Some people think that college athletes should not get paid.
They play for a big audience.

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
In response to the question asked, the graph at hand is split into 3 categories: Age, Race & Gender. Those older in age have a higher percentage of disagreement with colleges paying athletes. As the younger generations tend to agree with the payment idea proposed. Those who think highly of the idea are Blacks and Latinos, furthermore, women represented great disapproval of paying athletes compared to the representations from men. 
2) What do you wonder?
Of those asked "Should colleges pay their athletes?" were their interests taken into consideration? In other words, do they have any relation to the athletic field or was the poll group chosen randomly?
What is the reasoning behind those who disagree with athletes being paid?
How do the 3 categories chosen influence opinions on this matter? 
3) How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community as there is a great range of people who intend to pursue athletics in college. 
4) What’s going on in this graph?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I notice that as the age increases more people say that colleges should not pay their athletes. As age increases more people also say that they are unsure. More men also believe that colleges should pay their athletes most likely because most of the college sports that would have pay would be for the male sports.

What do you wonder?

I wonder what the thought process is behind not wanting the college athletes to be payed? I also wonder why there are such differences in belief through age, race, and gender? I also wonder to what extent this impacts college athletes and weather. I also wonder how much the athletes would get paid and if they would get paid based on value to the team like the pros?

How does this relate to you and your community?

raw_comment:
1. I noticed a younger demographic of people feel as if college should pay their athletes, and as the older they get, the more people think they shouldn't be paid.  More Black and Latinos believe their athletes should be paid, while more White people believe they shouldn't be paid.  Also more men want athletes to be paid than women.

2.  I wonder why these certain groups want athletes to be paid.  Since college athletes would range from 18 to early 20's on average, it makes sense that demographic would want athletes to be paid.  While the older demographic would already have stable jobs or be retired, and not see the need to pay their athletes.

3. When it comes to my community, we range from low-middle class families, so a lot of students could use athletic scholarships to enter a good college for a lesser amount of money.  I would assume a large majority of my community would love to be paid by their college for the sport they play.

4. "Should Colleges Pay Up for their Athlete's Touchdowns?"

raw_comment:
1. I notice that there are bigger percentages of the students saying yes rather than no. I also noticed little to none were not sure about the question asked. The graph is also divided into different groups, age, race, and gender. 

2. I wonder how come a great percentage of elders, women, and white people are against college paying their athletes. If they were athletes in college, wouldn't they want to get paid for what they play? Wouldn't it be some sort of "reward" for all the efforts they put into the sport and it could kick off their career while also making a living in a way throughout college. 

3. This relates to me and my community because I know a few kids want to move onto playing sports in college or some have already. And I'm curious to see how they may feel about this poll. 

4. This graph is divided into three categorical groups (age, race, gender) to determine what each group votes regarding whether or not college athletes should get paid by the school they play/go to.
Headline: Should Money Be Put in the Pockets of College Athletes?

raw_comment:
1. I notice that in the first category of age, as respondents get older, a higher percentage of them say that colleges shouldn’t pay their athletes. From 18 to 29, 70% say yes, from 30 to 44, 57% say yes, from 45 to 59, 36% say yes, and from 60 and older, 29% say yes. It can also be seen that while people who are black and latino equally agree that colleges should pay their athletes at 69%, the amount of white people who agree with them is much less at 34%. There is also a divide in gender that can be seen with 54% of male respondents saying the athletes should be paid and 39% of female respondents saying they should be paid.
2. I wonder why as the age of the respondents increases, the amount of people who say student athletes should be paid by their colleges becomes lower, is it due to the time period they were born in, or is it something else? Similarly, I wonder why people who are white are much less in agreement with people who are black and latino in terms of colleges paying their athletes. I wonder if it was a result of not having as big of a sample of white people as there was of black and latino people, and if it might be the same thing for the percentages regarding the males and females.
3. This relates to my community and I because there are many senior athletes in the school that would benefit greatly from going to college after graduating and being able to be paid for playing a sport that they’re good at and enjoy playing.
4. Do College Athletes Deserve Payment?

raw_comment:
1. I discovered that while older Black and Latino males prefer to believe that colleges shouldn't pay athletes for college, younger Black and Latino males tend to have the opposite opinion. This is probably due to the age difference, when college sports were less common. But I also observe that people my age aren't in college, so they probably think differently about whether or not college athletes should get paid.

2. I'm curious as to why so many elderly folks think colleges shouldn't pay their players. I also wonder why more women than men advocated against universities paying their athletes; perhaps this is because women are aware that sportsmen are more likely to receive higher salaries and that colleges are more willing to support male athletes than those who are female.

3. Since many people are in their final years of high school and will soon be attending college, I can relate this to them. Significant changes may wind up being relevant by the time we are in college because younger generations are preferring the idea of colleges paying their student athletes more and more.

4. "Should Student Athletes Be Paid, or Play For Free?"

raw_comment:
1.In the graph I notice that there is a trend of as the age groups got older, the people believe less and less that athletes deserve to be paid by their colleges. I also notice that the largest population of people unsure were in the age group of over 60. When it comes to race, black and latinos both have 69% of their population thinking college athletes deserve to be paid, while white people only have 34%. Next I noticed that majority of women answered no. 
2.I wonder if the reason older people were more likely to say no to collegiate athletes being paid was because if they were athletes in college they didn't get paid, and therefore they see no reason for people in college now to get this. I also wonder why in the age groups of 45-59 and 60 up the same percent said no but much more were undecided in the 60 and older group. Lastly I question if the reason much less white people(compared to the poc) said yes to athletes and pay was because of the economic gap between white people and black and latinos in America. 
3.This relates to me and my community because as a senior in highschool me and my classmates are preparing for our lives in college. This for some people may include being an athlete either for enjoyment, scholarships or for both, therefore this argument of collegiate athlete pay directly affects my age group. This also affects low-income students who would benefit drastically from pay while competing on a college team. 
4.Making Bands while making baskets.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I notice that as the age increases more people say that colleges should not pay their athletes. As age increases more people also say that they are unsure. More men also believe that colleges should pay their athletes most likely because most of the college sports that would have pay would be for the male sports.

What do you wonder?

I wonder what the thought process is behind not wanting the college athletes to be payed? I also wonder why there are such differences in belief through age, race, and gender? I also wonder to what extent this impacts college athletes and weather? I also wonder how much the athletes would get paid and if they would get paid based on value to the team like the pros?

How does this relate to you and your community?

This relates to me because many of the people I know played on college sports teams. There are also a many high schoolers I know that are planing or have gotten athletic scholarships.

raw_comment:
1.The graph has been broken into three sections: race, ethnicity, and age. I noticed that in the age category, those who are 60 or older disagreed that colleges should pay their athletes, while the younger they are the more likely they are to agree similar to the other groups like minorities and men.  I also noticed that women disagreed more than men. This has me believing that the inequality within colleges, especially in sports, is playing a huge input in why women would feel the need to disagree due to the fact that men already have been given more opportunities than what they've been trying to earn. Moreover, as generations go by, the younger they are the stronger they believe in their worth and time. Hence why several of them agreed to colleges paying their athletes. 
2.I wonder if the data was collected from past and present college athletes. To put it into other words, when asked, for example, were the 60-year-olds past college athletes, or were they random 60-year-olds just randomly asked? Same thing for the "Gender" data. Were the men and/or women being asked also college athletes, college students, or random people?
3. This relates to my community as there are several students who are planning to continue their athletic careers in college. Sadly I am not an athlete, but I am not blind to the fact of how little women are hyped for college sports. This graph further proves it. 
4. HEADLINE: 
Athletes Win and Lose...Yet at What Cost?

raw_comment:
1. The closer that the participants are, to the age of athletes at the college level, have the least opposition to payments. Specifics are unclear, for what the source of payment is, making the question simpler to dictate a yes-or-no answer upon; it reflects the perspective of how each age group sees this idea. College students are associating money as a benefit, based on the glorification of being paid. The more experience with age, creates the factor of how it may be either unnecessary or lead to other unhealthy habits with money. The older the age group, the less they are for payments. 

2. I wonder if there were specifics or if the question was worded differently, how different groups would respond. For example if they were to make money based on promoting their team on social media, or there was income coming from work that the athletes do in order to benefit the team's fan base and respect. Would this alter all of the responses, or create the same distribution?

3. This relates to sports in my town, as a cluster association for each individual team. They each have their own specific way to make money to by equipment or warm up clothes for games, and they have to find ways to get that profit, it isn't granted by the school aside from the basic needs for the sport.

4. The graph is skewed to the right, the right being the older people, the right being the white people, and the right being women. "We should pay the college athletes! But at what cost?"

raw_comment: I notice younger people are more supportive of paying college athletes. So are those from minority races and men. I wonder if this support is related to wealth, as poorer people are perhaps more likely to support additional avenues of moneymaking. I can't say this graph relates to me or my community, however, as I am a high school student and don't go to college. Finally, perhaps a catchy line for this graph is "the younger you are, the more likely you support paying college athletes."

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who participated!

Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  "Split Views on Paying College Athletes" by Finn and Olivia of Cookeville, Tennessee; “Should Athletic Commitment Come with Pay?” by Janay of Philadelphia; “Paid to Play?  Or Not Today?” by Danaher of Berkley, Michigan; “College Athlete Compensation: Yes or No?” by Sophia of Andover High School in Massachusetts; "Should College Athletes Be Making Bucks" by Diego, and "Are Scholarships Enough to Pay Our Star Athletes?" by Bryn and Edwin of Eaglecrest High School in Aurora, Colorado.

You can continue to post comments and replies.  Please check back on Friday. November 18th when we will reveal the free link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graph, and a few Stat Nuggets.

There will be no graph during the week of Thanksgiving.  But, we will post the graph for the November 30th moderation on Friday, November 18th.  The topic – U.S. life expectancy by group.

raw_comment:
A trend I noticed in the graph shows younger people along with Black and Latinos agreeing more on the idea that college athletes should be paid based on percentage. The graph also reflects the higher percentage of men who agree with the idea that college athletes should be paid.  

Something which I wonder is why older people tend to believe that college athletes should not be paid, whereas younger people believe otherwise. Part of the curiosity comes from the potential idea that the older generation believed similarly to those of the younger generation at some point, but a change could have changed the belief.

The issue about whether college athletes should be paid relates to my community as it is an issue to where it reflects that despite students being able to get jobs related to the college itself and get paid, student athletes still do not get compensated for their performances. Some college athletes may need the pay in order to help with the family, as the growing need for pay with some athletes becomes an issue with one finding it harder to avoid college, affecting my community and the future generations when it is not guaranteed for pay, unless one gets endorsements.

In the graph, it shows the percentage of people, in a specific group, who either agree, disagree, or are unsure on whether college athletes should be paid. A headline which could be catchy in grabbing the attention of the audience is “Younger population in favor of college athletes getting paid!”

raw_comment:
I noticed that younger people (those under the age of 44 years) make up more than half of the yes percentage on the age graph. Many of those older than 44 voted no making up more than half of the no percentage on this graph. The older the age group, the more people who vote no. Younger people are more affected by this question because they are the ones who are currently in or just graduated college. This may bias their opinion because they are already spending a lot of money to go to college for their studies and are taking in a whole new commitment. Unlike older generations, younger generations have been more focused on college athletics. More men then women also voted yes on this graph. I think this is due to more men playing college sports than women. College women's sports have not always existed and many colleges still don't have select women sports. They may feel men are already having an opportunity they may not have so why should they get paid for it too. 
I wonder how these people in the survey were chosen. Did they all go to college? Did they all play a college sport?
This relates to my community because many of my friends and I are high school athletes looking to make it to the college level. This may upset those who do play a sport at the college level and find out colleges are no longer paying athletes even though they paid those just a few years older than them. 
Headline: Price of a College Athlete

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
From looking at this graph, I notice more black and latino men and women want colleges to pay athletes in comparison to white men and women. Around 69% of both black and latino citizens want colleges to pay their students while only 34% of white citizens are in support of it. 
 
What do you wonder?
From this graph, I wonder why the support for colleges paying their athletes differs when it comes to surveying different ethnicities, genders, and ages. I also wonder how many of those surveyed are college athletes, since I feel that would definitely have an affect on their opinion. 
 
What’s going on in this graph?
In this graph, it represents the public's opinion on whether college athletes should be paid for their participation in college sports. The graph illustrates the responses in three different categories; one bar graph represents the responses between men and women, one represents the responses between black, white, and latino men and women, and the last represents the responses between different ages. 
 
How does this relate to you and your community?
This graph relates to me because I am a senior in high school and this issue is something I personally have an opinion on. It is a topic that I will face in only a couple months and it is helpful to know what the differing opinions are. 
 
Headline: College Athletes: Deserving of Pay?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that younger people, who are in college or just out of college, are more likely to believe that college athletes should get paid. I also noticed that more Black and Latino people think that colleges should pay athletes compared to white people. More men thought that college athletes should get paid than women. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder how race and gender affect the answer to this question. 
Do more people of color go to college for sports than white people? Do more men go to college for sports compared to women? 

How does this relate to you and your community?
I am applying to colleges right now, and I have friends who will be college athletes. I think this is an important discussion, especially if college students plan to pursue a sport as a full-time career. 

What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
College athletes: Having Fun or Working Hard?

raw_comment:
I notice that this graph depicts the demographics of how people respond to the question, "Do you think colleges should pay their athletes?" The people answering the survey whose ages range from 18 to 29 and and 30 to 44, made up of over half the percentage, voting that colleges should pay their athletes.  the people from the ages 45 to 59 and 60 or older believed that colleges should not pay their athletes. This may be because most of the athletes they would be paying are in the age range of 18 to 29 and they have stronger beliefs that they should be getting paid. the Black and Latino were even in agreement that athletes should be getting paid my their colleges. I also notice that more women do not think that athletes should be paid. 
I wonder whether the people being asked are athletes going to college or not athletes, or whether they are going to college at all. 
This relates to me and my community because it may upset the college students who are not being funded, but might need it. Whereas, some athletes who are not in need of college funding are being provided it.

What do you notice? 
When I look at the graph, I notice that the younger the person is, the more likely is that person to think that colleges should pay their athletes. Most White people believe that colleges should not pay their athletes while most Black and Latino people think that colleges should pay their athletes. About half of all men would like athletes to be paid by their colleges, while most women think that athletes should be paid. 

What do you wonder? 
I wonder why there is such a big difference between the black, Latino and white. 

How does this relate to you and your community? 
Being paid as a college student athlete would help them, because college students are often already poor and have to work after college or on the weekends. When they play a sport, they have less time to do that.

raw_comment:
1) I saw that as the age groups became closer together, people were less likely to say yes when asked if college players should be compensated. I also noted that males in this study were more likely to answer yes, while females said no more frequently.

2) I wonder how many (if any) athletes were included in the case study, and how that would affect the results. I wonder if there is a reason as to why the Black and Latino ethnic group want college athletes to be payed more than the white ethnic group? I'm also curious how this study relates to the whole population of US adults, and whether it's an accurate picture of the population.

3) Some people devote time and money to their sports careers prior to and through college, but the majority of college players still spend a lot of money to play. As my peers began to commit to or participate in college athletics, the subject became more pertinent. It shouldn't be that universities profit off of athlete's likenesses without compensation to their players. As a resident of Perth Amboy, it is nice to see support being given to the players.

4) Play for Pay: The Schism on Athletic Endowment

raw_comment:
I noticed that… The youngest respondents to the survey believe that college athletes should be paid and as respondents age increase they are more apprehensive of athletes being paid. I also noticed that almost twice as many minorities, blacks and latinos, believed that college athletes should be paid compared to white respondents. Men also said a higher percentage of college athletes should be paid. 
 
I wonder if… The motivations of money will shift the culture of youth sports and that parents will push their children now to not just get a college scholarship, but to also earn an income. I also wonder whether the divide between female athlete income and male athlete incomes will continue to divide if colleges aren’t equitable in their paychecks.
 
This relates to my community because… I am a student athlete myself, but I take part in running that doesn’t even pay much at the professional level. I know that colleges paying athletes may help some other sports such as football, but track and cross country will most likely not benefit from such an endow. 
 
My name for this graph would be… “At What Cost Do We Support Collegiate Athletes?”

I wonder if there are other variables at play such as income? That could be a good variable to include. Also, why do only 39% of women think college athletes should be paid?
This could relate to some of my friends/people I know who are athletes trying to play in college.

raw_comment: I notice that younger people, men, and minorities tended to favor the idea that colleges should pay their athletes. This makes sense because younger people, ages 18-29 are more likely to empathize with college athletes because they are closer to them in age. People who are Black and Latino also show to agree that colleges should pay their athletes. Blacks and Latinos are often minorities that struggle to pay for college, so having colleges pay their athletes, especially those that are diverse could help someone who can't afford college. I also notice that Men favor the idea more than women. I wonder why men answer yes more than women do. I also wonder what possible confounding factors there are when gathering information for this graph. Is it possible that the population was made up of all men and women leaving a college basketball game? These factors can affect the outcome of the graph. This relates to me because as someone entering college and as an avid sports fan, I have been paying attention to the recent allowance for college athletes to be paid. Furthermore, a friend of mine will be attending UNC next year as an athlete and this could greatly affect her experience. My headline: "Should Colleges Give Back What Athletes Put In?"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that people as people get older they start to think that athletes should not be paid for playing in college or they become more unsure about what to do. Along with this, black and Latino people generally think that these athletes should be getting paid while white people are more in the middle. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder if the older people who said that athletes shouldn't be getting paid believe that more because they aren't the ones experiencing college since they are likely past that point in their lives. 
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because many people go to college for sports so it affects the people around me. 
What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
A headline could be "The Future Income of College Athletes?"

raw_comment:
1.What do I notice?
-The smallest percentiles are unsure across all different demographics. 
-The groups who most thought athletes should get paid in college were 18-29 years olds, the Black community, the Latino community and men. 
-This issue is surprisingly divisive, as few people were unsure and most percentages for yes or no were relatively close. 
2.What do I wonder? 
-Why are women less likely to think college athletes should be paid, despite the fact that women often face the brunt of discrimination in athletics? 
-Does age have a direct correlation with opinions on this issue? 
-What led to the Black and Latino community having equal percentages of opinion on this issue? 
-What caused the 60 or older group to have the most people unsure about their opinion on the issue? 
3.What do I think is going on in this graph? 
I think this graph is showing the opinions of various age groups, ethnicities, and genders on whether or not college athletes should be paid by their college. 
4.How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to me and my community as I know of a few people who will be going to college and playing a sport. Their opinion would most likely be that college athletes should be paid by the school which they attend. Also, the opinions shown in this graph (especially regarding the men and 60 or older categories) reflect heavily what I have heard in my own life and in my community. 
5.Headline
"Argument over Athletics: Should Colleges pay athletes?"

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
I notice that it appears that people in the younger age group ( 18-19) tend to think colleges should pay their athletes and the percentage of people in the age group saying yes to paying college athletes continuously declines the older the age group. I also noticed that Black and Latino people had a higher percentage of people voting yes to college athletes getting paid than White people did. More men said college athletes should get paid than women. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder why the percentage of people who think athletes should get paid declines as the age group gets older and why most women and White people don’t think college athletes should be paid, but a majority of men, Black, and Latino people thought athletes should get paid.  
 How does this relate to you and your community? 
Whether or not college athletes get paid influences their financial stability. I know some athletes are only able to play in college because they are receiving money they need to pay for their college and living expenses. 
What’s going on in the graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main ideas. 
The graph shows the percentage of people from different ages, races, and genders that thought whether or not college athletes should get paid. “Do athletes in college need to get paid?”

I notice that as people get older, they appear less supportive of college athletes being paid, and that there is significant difference between the opinions of men and women.

I wonder why women are less supportive of college athletes getting paid than men.

I know people who will be collegiate athletes in the future, and this could affect whether or not they get paid.

raw_comment:
I notice that those who are younger, thus either in or recently having gone to college, are more likely to say that college athletes should be paid. It was also more common for people of a minority to say ‘yes’ to the question. Men were also more likely than women to say ‘yes’.
I would like to know the location the survey took place as it could greatly affect answers. I would also like to know the amount of each group surveyed.
Many of my peers are going to college on athletic scholarships, thus it could affect certain elements of their college experience whether or not they were getting paid.
The graph compares the distribution of answers to the question “should college athletes be paid?” based on various attributes of the people surveyed. These attributes include Race, Gender, and Age. It shows that, usually, someone is more likely to say yes if they are a minority, male, and of a young age.

1. What do you notice? 
I noticed that the older people who voted and shared their opinion were more on the no side of colleges paying their athletes, and that the younger people 18-29 voted mostly that college athletes should get paid.

I wonder what the circumstances of this wage would be. Would Men and Women get paid the same? Would different sports get different amounts of money? Can most colleges and universities afford this?
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This impacts my community because many of my friends/ family members play collegiate sports. They would be making money during college without having to work a generic job.

This graph shows the opinions of people ages 18 and up, different race/ethnicities, and genders, on whether or not college athletes should be getting paid.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I notice that people of ages 18-29 mainly believe that colleges should pay their athletes. This could be because they are athletes and know that their efforts should not only be appreciated, but also paid for. I also notice that very little people are unsure because most have strong opinions about colleges paying their athletes. 

2. What do you wonder?
I wonder what made each person come up with their decision about colleges paying their athletes. I also wonder why women don't believe that athletes should be paid by the colleges. 

3. How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to the student athletes in my school. They work really hard to balance work, school and sports to be able to gain attention from colleges. Colleges will then notice them and use their hard work to gain more attention for themselves. Colleges should atleast pay them for all the stress that they will go under. 

4. Student Athletes: Do They Deserve to be Paid?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
In the graph, I noticed that there are multiple variables contributing to the data: Age, Race/Ethnicity, and Gender. There seems to be an association between paying college athletes and all of the variables. For instance, the younger the person is, the more likely they are to agree with paying student athletes or men tend to be more agreeing of paying student athletes than women. For direct proof of association, however, you would need more statistical proof.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why people of color tend to agree more with paying student athletes than white people? Is it because of a certain trend in the diversity of student athletes at the college they attended or is due to some other lurking variable?

How does this relate to you and your community?
I come from a college town and while I don't know any college athletes, I do know that they are just kids. Kids that went to the same high school as me and take the same college classes as some of my friends, and if they're sacrificing their time and efforts that could be going to their schoolwork for a sport, then why shouldn't they be getting paid?

raw_comment:
What do you notice? I notice that the older generations–as you go up–have a larger majority than previous ones who believe that colleges shouldn’t pay their athletes as well as are more unsure of how to answer the question, “Do you think colleges should pay their athletes?” Also, a majority of men said yes to this question as compared to the minority who answered this that were women. Out of all ethnicities questioned, whites have the largest percentage of individuals answering no with Black and Latino having an equal percentage of people answering yes (although they don’t have an equal percentage saying no or that they are unsure).
What do you wonder? I wonder how this data was collected: how many people of each group were questioned and whether each was questioned equally. I also wonder why a majority of white respondents said no.
How does this relate to you and your community? This relates to me due to the fact that people I know and who are in my community are athletes. Therefore, some of them may consider continuing their athletic career in college if they are paid, and the answers people give in polls like this could affect whether or not that happens. Also, I and everyone else has opinions about this debate.

raw_comment:
What do I notice
The purple portion of the graph represents those who agree that colleges should pay their athletes. The orange portion represents those who do not believe that colleges should pay their athletes. The gray portion represents those who are unsure. The graph also covers the responses of three different demographics according to age, race/ethnicity, and gender.

What do I wonder?
I wonder what portion of those who were polled are/were college athletes and how that impacted their responses.

What do I observe?
I observed that those who agree that colleges should pay their athletes decreases with age. For instance, 70% of those ages 18-29 agreed that colleges should pay their athletes. However, only 29% of people 60 or older agreed that said that they should pay their college athletes. This is likely because people between 18-29 contains all those who this issue is most likely relevant to. Similarly those who are black or Latino are 35% more likely to agree that colleges should pay their athletes compared to white individuals. 54% of men are also shown to be in favor of college's paying their athletes, while only 39% are in favor.

How it relates to my community
This issue is relevant to me because I am currently in the college application process and I know many people who are committing to school for a sport.

1. I noticed that as the interval of the age groups increased, they were less likely to have responded yes when posed with the question of whether or not college athletes should be paid. I also noticed that the males in this survey were more likely to respond yes, while females more frequently responded no to the question.

3. This relates to me and my community as I am at or near the subject of interest (college athlete) and is a very much prevalent topic in the college sports world community, whether or not student athletes should receive NIL deals. We may also see an increase in the amount of talent and skill needed to be successful on the collegiate level, as NIL incentives will cause increased student participation.
4. A catchy headline would be  "The College Athlete Pay Divide: To Pay or not to Pay, that is the Question"

What do you notice?
I notice that most people believe that student athletes should be payed especially the younger generation.
What do you wonder?
I wonder why the race and ethnicity really determines if athletes should be payed the same. Also wonder why men athletes should be payed more than women
How does this relate to you and your community?

I noticed that more men(54%) thought that college athletes should be paid then woman 39%. I also noticed that as people got older the amount of people who agreed college athletes should get paid went down. I think that possibly could be because the age group of 18 to 29 makes up the majority of college students so they were the most in favor if them being paid.
What do you wonder? I wonder why black and latino people said yes to athletes being paid at a rate 2 time higher then what white people said. 
How does this relate to your community? This effects my community because some of my peers may have excelled enough in their respective sport to be offered division one scholarships. I think high school students would say yes to this question at a higher percentage then say people ages 45 to 59 because college is more important in their life and some may have the opportunity to get paid for college sports.
What going on in this graph? They are displaying percents of people who are for and against college athletes getting paid and dividing it by age, race and gender.
Catchy headline: College Athletes; Pay or Play?

raw_comment: The graph for today was made from a Marist poll with 1,264 people involved. Age, race, and gender are all factors in whether they agree if colleges should pay athletes. In our findings, we found that typically the younger the person the more they agree with the idea of paying college athletes. The rates of the vote “yes” drop from 70% (ages 18-29) to 29% (age 60 or older). Another finding we found interesting was the racial and ethnicity graph. There is a considerable difference between people of color and white people if they voted yes or not. One other factor to consider is the gender factor. Unsurprisingly, men voted yes more than women did. There are already many more opportunities for men in the sports field than there arefor women. Everyone knows the wage gap between male and female athletes. All in all, the graph shows us whether certain age groups, genders, and ethnicities agree with the idea of paying college athletes.

raw_comment: This graph depicts different people's thoughts on whether or not college athletes should be paid. In general, the frequency of answering "yes" decreases with age. Additionally, I notice how people who are black or latino or more likely to say "yes" than people who are white. Men are also more likely to say "yes" than women. The age difference could be because some of the younger people who responded to this poll may be college athletes themselves or be friends with college athletes. I wonder if the people surveyed would change their answer if they were/ were not college athletes. I wonder what their reasoning is for their answer. This graph relates to my community because I have a good friend who will be playing a D1 sport in college, which leads me to wonder further if collegiate athletes should be paid by their schools. A title for this graph could be, "College Athletics: Play without Pay?"

raw_comment: The headline we came up with was Should Colleges Pay Athletes or No? This graph and article’s main point is whether or not college athletes should get paid in addition to having a scholarship. Something we noticed was that the younger people seem to vote for student-athletes to receive salaries while the older people seem to disagree. Another thing is that Black and Latinos have a higher chance of supporting athletes getting paid. Lastly, we noticed that men seem to agree on the topic more than women. A wonder we had was why are older people and women more likely to be against the decision of payment. Another wonder we had was why there is a large gap between white and Black/Latino individuals. An impact this topic has on our community is the decision to attend college through sports because attending college for 4 years can change people’s minds when it comes to money.

raw_comment:
I've noticed that the older generation had a higher percentage of people who didn't think athletes should be paid for sports, and that the younger generation was largely more in support of athletes being paid. The other thing that stood out to me was that in the women category there was a larger percentage of women who were opposed to athletes being paid. 

I wonder why there were more white people that were opposed to athletes being paid. I also wonder why there was a larger percentage of women who were opposed to athletes being paid. I wonder the thought process of these women, and why they didn't want college athletes to be paid. I also wonder if they were thinking about both women's and male sports, and if that means that they're not in support of women being paid. 

I know people that play D1/D3 sports. College athletes dedicate a lot of time and work to playing their sport, so it makes sense that they should be paid for the time and work they put in. 

College Athletes; Play but no Pay

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that the youngest age group of 18-29 want college athletes to be payed the most. I think this is because they are the age of the college athletes and relate more to them. The oldest age group or 60 or older think the most that they should not be payed. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why the the Black and Latino ethnic group want college athletes to be payed more than the white ethnic group. Does it have to do with income?

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community because allowing college athletes to be paid will make playing sports in college even harder because there will be more of a demand. This will effect younger athletes who are aiming to play sports in college. It will also increase the cost of college because they need money to pay their athletes.

raw_comment:
What I notice: As you look at the people in the youngest group to the oldest, the percent of people saying yes goes down from 70% to 29%. I think there was response bias from the youngest group because some of them may be college athletes at the time of being asked this question. That same bias can apply to older people ages 60 or older because they are more likely further removed from college and don't care about the question as much.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why less white people say no and less women say no to college athletes getting paid. This may be because there are more  men division one athletes the women(roughly 280,000 to 225,000 in 2020).

What impact does this have on you and your community?
I don't believe these viewpoints heavily affect our community because this debate is really only applying to division one schools. There will be a few outliers every now and then but the majority of our high school athletes that go to the next level play in division two or three schools.

I noticed that as people got older, they were less likely to think colleges should pay athletes. Also, I
noticed that a very small percentage of all the people surveyed were unsure. It was interesting to see what
different races and genders felt about the subject.

I wonder why typically older people don't support colleges paying athletes.

It impacts me and my community because athletes that are looking to pursue careers in sports that are
going into college next year, can start making earnings for themselves and their families. Being an athlete
can be very time-consuming so making money outside of their sport can be difficult.

Discordance Between College Athletes Being Paid

1. What do you notice?
When looking at the race you can see that Black or Latino people are more likely to say yes than white people, it is probably because black people and Latinos make up more of the sports population than white people. Sports is also used as a tool to get out of rough neighborhoods so if college students can make
money in that sport it will help their families.

Are the people over 65 saying no because they didn't get paid when they were in college, out of spite or how things used to be, or is it because they think that college athletes shouldn't be paid?

It will impact my community because if athletes are getting paid I feel as though they will be more likely to finish college rather than run to the big leagues to try and get money. It also might provide better performance because you know that you are getting paid the better you do not only for an award, for the team
and school.
