raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
-I noticed that a large majority of younger Black and Latino males believe that colleges should pay athletes for college, while those who are older tend to believe that colleges shouldn't pay athletes most likely because of the age difference when college in sports was less common. However, I also notice that those of older age aren't in college and therefore they most likely have different beliefs about whether college athletes should be paid.

2) What do you wonder?
-I wonder why a lot of older people believe that colleges shouldn't pay their athletes. I also wonder why older people tend to disagree more with college athletes getting paid. Do you think this is due to the fact that when they were in college it was a lot cheaper than it is now?

3) How does this relate to you and your community?
-This is relevant to me and my community because many high school athletes, like myself, may have looked for ways to join a college team in order to secure scholarships. Many people have this as their major objective because they may not have enough money to pay for tuition and their entire school. Minorities and students from disadvantaged backgrounds would experience less financial stress if student-athletes were paid.

4) What’s going on in this graph?
-"College Athletes Cost More than the Season"

raw_comment:
What do I notice: I notice when you look at the first age demographic, the answer yes slowly decreases as the age increases. This could be because younger college athletes would most likely answer yes and the older group would answer no because of either they were athletes and weren't paid or they are heads of the university and don't want to pay them.

What do I wonder: I wonder if people don't want to pay because of the fact that mainly male sports would bring in the most revenue and the amount of publicity the college has. For the most part I wonder if they also don't want to pay because of the fact they would have to pay female athletes as well.

How does this relate to me and my community: This relates to me because as a high schooler, student athletes are worried about getting an athletic scholarship to get to college. The financial side is a huge influence when they get offers from colleges so this would be a major impact if colleges pay their athletes.

My headline: Athletes vs. Colleges, The Rival Match of the Year

raw_comment: This graph demonstrates the opinions of different groups regarding whether or not college athletes should be paid a salary.  The main thing that sticks out is that younger people ages 18 to 29 are more likely to agree with this than someone who is older than 60.  This is probably due to the fact that this age group is in college or graduated recently and have a higher chance of being affected by or caring about this.  Black and Latino people also agree with this idea more than White people, and men approve of it more than women.  I wonder what the cause of these divides is.  I wonder if it has something to do with the fact that a lot of major college sports are male-dominated, like football.  This relates to my community because most people I know enjoy college sports.  It offers some form of entertainment for people, so the argument that athletes should be paid is rather valid.  I would entitle this graph: "Approval of College Athlete Salary."

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that the older generations, for the most part, do not think college athletes should be paid, whereas the younger generations, who are in the primary age group of college students, mainly think college athletes should be paid. I also notice that the majority of men believe college athletes should be paid, whereas the majority of women do not think college athletes should be paid.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why the majority of women do not believe college athletes should be paid. I also wonder why the majority of whites do not believe college athletes should be paid.

How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to me because a couple of my friends are current college athletes. This relates to my community because some of my high school friends are applying to be college athletes.

Title: Should college athletes have lower tuition, or get paid?

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graphs display the February 15 – 21, 2022 Marist poll which asked whether college athletes should be paid.  At issue is whether college athletes are employees of their universities.  Some believe that if athletes were paid, this would encourage athletes to cheat and this would affect sports betting.  

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?”, “What do you wonder?"  and “How will this affect you?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in these graphs. We look forward to replying to your discoveries.

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the online article that included these graphs.  

Note that you can get a link to your response (and replies made to it) to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

 The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, Nov. 18 with moderation on Wednesday, Nov. 30.  The topic – Covid by Group.

4. What's going on is people are placed into different categories and evaluated based on their answers to the question.
"Should college athletes be getting paid? You decide."

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I see that the responses are divided into age, Race/Ethnicity, and Gender, with Yes, No, and Unsure being the options for each. Regarding age, younger respondents were more likely to believe universities should compensate student-athletes, while older respondents were less likely to agree. In terms of race, more Black and Latino voters chose "yes" than "no." Finally, males were more likely than women to believe that colleges should compensate their athletes.

What do you wonder?
I'm curious as to why significantly more Black and Latino people than White people believe that colleges should compensate their student-athletes. I also wonder why the percentages for men and women differ so significantly.

How does this relate to you and your community?
Since many people in the neighborhood are in their final years of high school and will soon be attending college, I can relate this to them. Significant changes may wind up being relevant by the time we are in college because younger generations prefer the idea of colleges paying their student-athletes more and more.

What’s going on in this graph?
College athletes: do they deserve the money? or Are college athletes really worth it?

raw_comment:
I noticed that a large majority of younger Black and Latino males believe that colleges should pay athletes for college, while those who are older tend to believe that colleges shouldn't pay athletes most likely because of the age difference when college in sports was less common. However, I also notice that those of older age aren't in college and therefore they most likely have different beliefs about whether college athletes should be paid.

I wonder why a lot of older people believe that colleges shouldn't pay their athletes. I also wonder why more women said that colleges shouldn't pay their athletes than men, I wonder if it's because women know that sportsmen are more likely to be paid more and colleges are more likely to pay for athletes that are male rather than those who are female.

I don't play sports, nor am I interested in it but this relates to others in my community who want to go into a college for a sports-related career as they can think about whether they want to be paid by colleges for excelling at the sport.

A catchy headline for this graph can be "Paid College Athletes, the Ongoing Game."

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? 
I notice that responses are broken down into three categories: Age, Race/Ethnicity, and Gender, and for each, responses included Yes, No, and Unsure. In terms of age, more people on the younger side thought that colleges should pay student athletes, while percentages of yes answers gets less and less as the age range gets older. For race, Black and Latino both voted yes more than White. Lastly, more men thought that colleges should pay their athletes than women. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why the percentage of Black and Latino people who think that colleges should pay their student athletes is significantly more than the percentage of White people that do. I also wonder why there is a significant difference in the percentages for men and women. 
3. How does this relate to you and your community?
I can relate this to the community because, being in the later years of high school, many will be going to college soon. With the younger generations increasingly favoring the idea of colleges paying their student athletes, significant changes may end up becoming relevant in the time we are at college.

These People Think THIS About Giving Pay to College Athletes

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice? 
I notice that responses are broken down into three categories: Age, Race/Ethnicity, and Gender, and for each, responses included Yes, No, and Unsure. In terms of age, more people on the younger side thought that colleges should pay student athletes, while percentages of yes answers gets less and less as the age range gets older. For race, Black and Latino both voted yes more than White. Lastly, more men thought that colleges should pay their athletes than women. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why the percentage of Black and Latino people who think that colleges should pay their student athletes is significantly more than the percentage of White people that do. I also wonder why there is a significant difference in the percentages for men and women. 
3. How does this relate to you and your community?
I can relate this to the community because, being in the later years of high school, many will be going to college soon. With the younger generations increasingly favoring the idea of colleges paying their student athletes, significant changes may end up becoming even more relevant in the time we are at college.

raw_comment:
1) I see that the poll includes 1,264 adults, all of whom were living in the US. Additionally, I see a tendency among the younger generation to support paying student athletes. This may have its origins in the widely held belief that younger athletes will perform better during the sporting seasons and that these students will bring significant victories to the institutions they represent. However, the elder generation believes that young athletes shouldn't be compensated for their physical abilities. Ethnic groupings also differ significantly from one another.
2) I'm curious as to why so many people think that some racial groups should have more access to employment opportunities than others. Where does the ambiguity surrounding athlete compensation come from? Does the responses to the survey have anything to do with respondents' ages? Can the government's budget be strained by compensating athletes?
3) This is relevant to me and my community because many of the high school athletes, like myself, may have looked for ways to join a college team in order to secure scholarships. Many people have this as their major objective because they may not have enough money to pay for tuition and their entire school. Minorities and students from disadvantaged backgrounds would experience less financial stress if student athletes were paid.
4) “Should Athletic Commitment Come With Pay?”
    "Student-Athlete talent, a Debt Unpaid, Can The Young Demographic Change That?"

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
I noticed that, for age, as the groups got older the percent of people who thought colleges should pay their athletes decreased. For race, black and latino adults shared the same 69% (majority), agreeing with the compensation, whereas a majority of white adults disagreed. Between men and women, a majority of men said yes while a majority of women said no.
2) What do you wonder?
I wonder if we'll see more colleges agreeing to pay athletes and/or more students advocating for it, as it seems that younger generations are more for it.
3) How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community as we're a part of an evolving generation that ask for more fruits for their labor, especially young people of color who typically aren't properly compensated. 
4) What’s going on in this graph?
The graph displays data showing whether adults are various age groups, races, and sexes believe colleges should pay their athletes. My headline for this would be "Do College Athletes Deserve Compensation?"

raw_comment:
I notice that from all the listed ages, adults from ages 18-29 are the most in favor of paying college athletes. 70 percent of adults ages 18-29 believe college athletes should be paid. This is showing the percentage of specific categorical categories to show who is in favor of them paying college athletes and who is not in favor. The article interviewed people by race/ethnicity, gender, and age.
I wonder why males are more lenient towards paying college athletes than females. I believe that it would have made more sense if it was the other way around due to the fact women get paid less for major league sports versus the salary male athletes earn in the major leagues. I am still surprised how only 54% of
males believe that colleges should pay athletes; why isn't it more?

This relates to my community because Massachusetts was the third state to legalize national sports betting. This makes me wonder why athletes are not receiving some income from the betting season, especially football athletes in Fantasy Football and Men's College Basketball Leagues. As someone who has friends who bet on sports, it makes more sense if the players earned some sort of income for their successes.

College Athletes Cost More than the Season

This could be because of younger college athletes would most likely answer yes and the older group would answer no because of either they were athletes and weren't paid or they are head of the university and don't want to pay them.

The financial side is a huge influence when they get offers from colleges so this would be a major impact if colleges pay their athletes.

raw_comment:
This graph poses the question of whether or not athletes should be paid in college, the answers varying depending on which demographic was questioned. I noticed that this graph was disproportionately in favor of paying athletes when based off the answers of younger, black or Latinx, or male individuals. I wonder why this is the case, and in what ways these statistics were taken - in other words, where and how were the people surveyed on these questions that led to these results. This relates to me and my community because I'm looking into becoming a college athlete, and I have many friends who are either also looking into this or have already become college athletes. 
Headline: Athletes need Receipts!

raw_comment:
What we noticed:

Older generations seem to be more in favor of not paying college athletes. Perhaps this is because in their generation, college athletes were not so recognized/paid. More black people say "yes" to college athletes getting paid. Perhaps this is because black people have a harder time working towards becoming an athlete and feel they deserve compensation for their effort. More men agree with college athletes getting paid; perhaps this is because more men play sports than women. Sports tend to be targeted towards males. 

Catchy Titles: 
Wow: How Opinions on Getting Paid for College Sports Reveal Underlying Racism and Sexism in Sports.

raw_comment:
1.I saw that 1,264 adults, all of whom were in the US, were included in the poll. Additionally, the older people had been more unsure.Younger individuals feel that athletes should be paid more, whereas older ones say that athletes shouldn't be paid at all.While the majority of white people think colleges shouldn't pay its athletes, the majority of Latino and black people agree that they should.In terms of gender, more men than women support paying athletes.
2.I wonder if the survey pool had any factor in the survey.I wonder if they used an equal amount of people for each section such as the same amount of women and men, the same amount of 18-29-year-olds, and 45-59-year-olds.I wonder why the highest percentage of people who believe colleges should pay their athletes was 18-29-year-olds.I wonder if the graph had more diversity than just white, Latino, and black if it would alter or change the graph significantly. 
3.Because several of my friends are athletes and plan to do so in college, this affects both my community and me.Sports take up a lot of time, therefore I find it puzzling that people are not paid for such a time-consuming activity. I also know that because college is so costly, many students rely on scholarships, which occasionally center on sports. If sports are so time-consuming, that students are unable to find employment, they should be paid.
4.Shows the diverse nature behind paying college athletes."Full time athletes in college but unpaid? Make it make sense."

raw_comment:
1: I notice how the older the people are, the less that the majority thinks that colleges should pay their athletes.  I also notice how 10% of people 60 years or older are unsure of whether or not colleges should pay their athletes.  Along with that, the younger people get, the less the unsure percentage is.
2:  I wonder why there are more men who think colleges should pay their athletes compared to women and also why people who are older think that colleges shouldn't pay their athletes.
3: This relates to me and my community because if there is someone who wants to make a living off of a sport that they do, or if I do want to in the future, and that person doesn't currently have a way to make money, this would be a good option for them to choose.
4: I think what's going on in this graph is that in the past, the majority of people didn't play sports, or had good ways of making money instead of getting paid by the colleges for the sport that they played.  So people didn't think that they needed to be paid by the colleges for their sport.  But nowadays more people play sports or need money to support themselves so they think that colleges should pay college athletes.

raw_comment:
1.I notice that the age group of 18-29  and the race black and latino strongly believe that college should pay athletes but the older age group of 45 and older disagree on the same percentage just like the people that are white. Also, 2% more of women voted that colleges shouldn't pay athletes than the amount of men that voted yes. The age group of 18 to 29 and the latino group have the least unsure responses.
2. I wonder if the economic situation at home of the people asked to vote affected their response. For example, if someone comes from a family that struggles financially, might they think that athletes should get paid since they won't be able to work due to the games and practices. Also, might the older groups not think athletes should get paid because they might not see all the things athletes have to do to promote the schools on social media platforms.
3. This relates to my community because in my community there have been athletes that have made it to play college level and since they aren't able to work, I believe it interferes with their financial situations. My community is made up of families that aren't wealthy so if the student is playing sports, they are no longer able to have a job and help out with financial factors which is why I believe the latino group agreed very strongly for athletes to get paid.
4. The graph shows how age, race and gender might affect the thoughts on athletes being paid by the college. 

"Are They Going To Do It For The Money?"

raw_comment:
1. I've noticed that minorities based on age and ethnicity are more likely to agree that college athletes should be paid. This includes young adults aged 18 to 29, as well as black and Hispanics, who agree in large numbers with college athletes being paid to play outside of scholarships. The vast majority of men believe that college athletes should be compensated.
2. I'm curious why such a small percentage of white people believe college athletes should not be paid while such a large percentage of black and Latino people believe they should.
3. I believe the section of this chart involving gender relates to my community because I believe our schools prioritize male sports over female sports, and it stands to reason that males feel more entitled to be rewarded for participating in sports. Ethnicity also matters because we have a larger Latino and black community than whites who play sports, which may contribute to their desire to be compensated. Also, because these are low-income minority groups, it stands to reason that they are more concerned about their financial situations.
4. This graph shows the opinions of different categories of people and whether they believe athletes should be paid. "TO PAY OR NOT TO PAY".

They should get paid like it is.

raw_comment:
Colleges paying their athletes? I always thought it was the other way around. What I notice from the graph shown, is that younger people (ages 18-29), Latino & Black people, and men think colleges should pay their athletes. Older people (ages 60 or older), White people, and women have the least percentage agreeing with colleges paying their athletes. I wonder why Latino and Black people think this should happen and their percentages are the same. 
  This involves taking opinions, the chart needs more. More different groups of people to vote on this topic, this way we get different points of views from all sorts of people. In fact, I don’t see much relation to me there because of the lack of diversity. For younger people in high school and those who don’t even know much about sports. This graph shows the thoughts from few groups of people. A great headline would be “playing to play or to gain?” I don’t necessarily know what my opinion on this topic is but there are definitely other people my age who have thoughts and would like to take part in this. Personally I’d just do my own research and wonder if this will cause an incline in interest for playing a sport in college.

raw_comment:
A perfect example of why I don't always agree with the famous quote "Life's not fair." 
This graph is broken into 3 main stereotypes, then again with an additional 9 stereotypes: separating age, race, and gender. 

          Why is getting paid for a sport, or something many love and endure a career from, a stereotyped issue? I don't understand how it's fair to pay a white person far less than blacks and latinos if they are equal in skill. How is it fair to pay men further more than you're paying a woman? It seems like segregation all over again, and furthermore useless debates for people with way too much time on their hands. Why is this a new issue all of the sudden?

          I'm not big on sports, and in my community I don't hear about this much athletic segregation in my day to day life, fortunately. Yet it is common to hear a guy tell a girl the sport she plays isn't a real sport, because for example, in girls lacrosse tackling and checking sticks past a certain point is illegal, while for boys it's a part of their game of lacrosse. This is an understandable thing to debate about, yet it's unnecessary and not right to do. 

          This graph has the younger black/latino men getting the most gross earnings from the sports they play. To me, this is not fair. I thought we ended slavery years ago, so why reintroduce it to sports?

raw_comment:
I notice that people ages 18 to 29 , the age group of people in college, are the ones who think that they should get paid. And the older groups, especially ages 60 or older, say no. I also notice that the majority of men say they should be paid while the majority women say they shouldn't.
I wonder why these people think that. As a high schooler, I don't see the need to be paid, this is most likely due to the fact that my education is currently free. I also don't play a sport or plan to play a sport, so I don't have the same perspective as the people who do. One thing I would like to see added to this graph is another section of people who do and don't play sports to get another view point. I would assume that the people who play sports would say yes, but I think it would still be interesting to see. 
One idea that I agree with is that they may be compensated for their names, images, or likenesses to be used. I can understand how that would make sense. But to me, it would make sense for them to be paid by the people using those things. Now yes, it may be the colleges, but it may also be: news stations, magazines, newspapers, radio stations, and a few other places. 
The title I came up with is “To or To Not Get Paid? What College Athletes Think.”

raw_comment:
The Fiscal Rate of Athleticism
I hear this question float around the room at nearly all thanksgivings, evoking tight responses from each family member. This is what shocked me about the ten percent margin of 60 and older who were unsure, as my 75 year old grandpa seems to have a pretty good idea about it. That's the difference between theoretical and experimental; we base our theories off of our hypothetical experience(opinions), and experiments off of carrying out the hypothesis to the masses. 
For example, I could have theorized Men have a higher "yes" disposition than the Women (who have a higher "Unsure" disposition than men) due to the fact that I'm aware that society associates athleticism with masculinity. Now, just because I'm aware of this doesn't provide data evidence; I would need some sort of chart to prove my point, with percentages and visuals. Information from a chart I read in a textbook that displayed white people as more economically conservative to draw the conclusion that they would have the highest “No” rate when compared to other races.  This would be a good assignment where social studies students had to predict the demographics based on the question and the percentages, using synthesized information from class to apply to modern day polarizing questions.

Should colleges pay their athletes?
Who knew this one question could involve so many topics. In the graph given I see that is has been broken into 3 groups.

raw_comment:
Payroll. With each and every person in this graph their opinion varies depending on age, race, and gender. When looking towards different age groups younger people tend to stand with paying student athletes, when older folks are saying no. I see this and think the younger people would gravitate to paying them because that "is them". 70% voted on wanting students payroll while the older majority wouldn't have an effect on students being paid. They might even think it's pointless and a waste of school money which could be spent on education. 
Different race polls have Black and Latino people with the majority vote of payroll being given to student athletes. Depending on where you come from, these people may need to be paid for athletics to support their families or financial troubles. The White voters lean toward paying college athletes is almost half of the Black/Latina vote.

raw_comment: In this graph, I notice that up until age 45 the people supported colleges paying for their athletes, but after the answer switched to no. 70% of 18-29-year-olds said yes, 57% of 30-44-year-olds said yes, 36% of 45-59-year-olds said yes, and 29% of 60 or older said yes. I wonder why this is the trend. Why would older people not support colleges paying for their athletes? Why does the answer switch after age 45? This relates to me and my community because I am in High School and going to college in two years. It's important for me to know as a student how people view college payment because when I'm in college, there may be different policies than there are now. People's opinions change policies, if a lot of people don't support the payment, it may not occur in the future. Luckily, the amount of support and non-support is varied and most likely won't cause a major change now. I would name this, "Payment for Performance." The people are saying whether they support the payment for an athlete's performance.

raw_comment:
Evidence shows age, race/ethnicity, and gender impacting opinions
From ages 19-29, the youngest age bracket, 70% of people think that colleges should have paid athletes; most likely because they do not have a career or steady paycheck flowing in yet. So, they would not mind having some extra money earned from their talents to fall back on. In fact, my uncle, who was a college athlete 2 years ago, has talked to me about this topic saying that now, as he is trying to get a job, the extra cash would have been a good jump start to a career. This may be due to the number of male vs female athletes or because of inequality. However, there is not enough evidence in this graph to reflect any of the reasons given above; these are just possibilities. 

In my case, I do think that colleges should pay their athletes because of possible situations at home, extra money to help their future, and because they are helping the college earn money. Without the athletes, there would be no games, no revenue, and no earnings for the college.

raw_comment: The main purpose of this graph is to show what a different variety of people think about college athletes getting paid. I noticed that as the people get older, their responses tend to lean towards "no" and the younger people seem to vote "yes" as well as a majority of men picked "yes" while it was opposite for the women. I wonder why most of the women picked "no" since female athletes in general do not get paid equal or even near close to the men. Personally, I would pick "yes" since I am an athlete myself and plan to play football in college. I can see why most of the younger people picked "yes" because they're either an athlete in college, an upcoming athlete, or the group that watches college sports the most. The catchy title I decided to go with is Athletes and Accolades.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed as the ages get higher the amount of people saying yes goes down. I think that maybe because the older people have gone through college and may think it's not fair they didn't get paid for playing in high school, or maybe know more about why athletes shouldn't get paid. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder why the Race/Ethnicity rate for the white section is low. Why is there more Latino and Black votes and barely any White? 
How does this relate to you and your community?
I personally don't think this has much to do with my community and me, but I think it would be fair if colleges paid their athletes. Reason being these students are showing off their school making it draw peoples attention and creating popularity for the school. If these students didn't play the school probably wouldn't be as popular. 
What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
The graph is showing the rate of people voting for, "Do you think colleges should pay their athletes?"  The votes come from different genres like Age, Race/ Ethnicity, and Gender. In the age section the younger the age is the more votes Yes gets, but the older the age gets the more votes go to No. 
In the Race/Ethnicity section Black And Latino have more votes for Yes than White does. Lastly, the last section is Gender, out of Male and Female Male has more votes. 
"Pay or No Pay?"

I wonder why Black and Latino people think colleges should pay their athletes the same amount, but White people think colleges should pay their athletes less. I wonder if men think colleges should pay their athletes more than women because of stereotypes placed on men to be more athletic. 
This impacts me and my community because I know people who are going to be college athletes. I also know people who like to watch college games more than professional games. 
College Athlete Compensation: Yes or No?

raw_comment: The first thing that I noticed when looking at this graph is that people in younger age groups, like 18-29, are more likely to think that colleges should pay their athletes. Minority groups, specifically the Black and Latino communities also feel that colleges should pay their athletes. I figure that younger people feel that athletes should be paid because they are athletes themselves, and perhaps there is some bias there. I wonder why minority groups are more in favor of athletes getting paid? I wonder what a fourth variable, like income, would look like and how it would affect our view of the existing data. In my personal opinion, I think that athletes should not be paid by their colleges, but rather through things like sponsorships. Playing sports for their college is just one of the parts of attending the college itself; the college does enough just by allowing them to do so.

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 

The younger age demographics believe that college should pay their athletes, but as the age increases, that sentiment changes more with a lower percentage believing  that colleges should pay their athletes. I believe that college athletes should not be paid because they are representing so much more than themselves on the court. They are playing for their school, and uphold spirit. If colleges athletes are paid, they will have less of an incentive to play hard because they have nothing to work for. raw_comment: One of the biggest trends in the graph is the amount of college-aged people that agree to students being paid to participate in sports. This is because it affects them directly and would provide money for their current schooling, housing, and other commodities that they would need money for.
